rubric: PYTHON AS A FIRST LANGUAGE / FUNCTIONAL PROGRAMMING / CHAPTER 26

slides.title: Closures and decorators
slides.main: Create a function inside a function, and return it with its environment.

items.title: Decorator
items.sub: A function that improves a function

slides.title: Nested functions
slides.sub: Reading outer variables is fine; changing needs nonlocal
slides.main: A name is looked up in a chain: function, enclosing function, module, built-ins.

slides.title: Closure
slides.sub: A function takes its environment along
slides.main: The outer function has finished, but n lives on inside the inner one, like in a capsule.

body.text:
def make_multiplier(n):
    def mul(x):
        return x * n
    return mul

triple = make_multiplier(3)
five = make_multiplier(5)
print(triple(10), five(10))
print(triple.__closure__[0].cell_contents)

slides.title: State in a closure
slides.sub: Each factory call is its own capsule
slides.main: One method and a little state: a closure is shorter; several methods: a class is clearer.

body.text:
def make_counter():
    count = 0
    def inc():
        nonlocal count
        count += 1
        return count
    return inc

a, b = make_counter(), make_counter()
print(a(), a(), b())

slides.title: Late binding
slides.sub: A function remembers the variable, not the value
slides.main: Fix it with a default value, a factory or partial.

body.text:
funcs = [lambda: i for i in range(3)]
print([f() for f in funcs])
fixed = [lambda i=i: i for i in range(3)]
print([f() for f in fixed])

def make(i):
    return lambda: i

print([make(i)() for i in range(3)])

slides.title: The first decorator
slides.sub: Takes a function, returns a wrapper
slides.main: @name above def is shorthand: square = timer(square).

slides.title: Arguments and result
slides.main: Learn the template: inner function, call the original, return the result, return the wrapper.

slides.title: functools.wraps
slides.sub: So the name and docs aren't lost
slides.main: Decorate every decorator you write with @wraps.

slides.title: Decorator with parameters
slides.sub: One more level: a decorator factory
slides.main: Parentheses after the decorator name call a factory, not the decorator.

slides.title: A cache as a decorator
slides.main: Timing, logs, permissions, retries, handler registration: one line above the function.

slides.title: A class as a decorator
slides.main: Stacked decorators apply bottom up: the one nearest the function runs first.

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.sub: A forgotten return in the wrapper
slides.main: Check by hand: name = decorator(function) shows at once what you return.

body.text: Also: wrapper not returned, no @wraps, lambdas in a loop, decorator order, an over-clever decorator.

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: A closure is a function with an environment; a decorator is a closure that improves another function.
